Most UN General Assembly resolutions are recommendations whose value as a “source” is evidentiary: they can show or help form customary international law, especially opinio juris, when support is broad, the language is normative, and state practice aligns, as with the Friendly Relations Declaration. A narrow class binds under the Charter itself (budgetary and internal organizational decisions); the rest is soft law that may later harden into custom or treaty rules. “Always customary law” and “equivalent to treaties” both overstate that role.

CONFIDENCE: 92
